source_title: mutonby/agentring: Let your AI agents call your phone over VoIP, and call them back. Your phone rings like a real call, even locked; a voice AI talks it through and returns the transcript. Self-hosted, open source, no phone numbers or Twilio. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
Your AI agent can call you. When it needs a decision, hits a wall or finishes a long job, your phone rings like a real call, even locked and in Doze. A voice AI tells you what's going on, you talk it through, and the agent gets the transcript and carries on. You can also call your agents back from the app and ask them things by voice.
Self-hosted and open source. No phone numbers, no Twilio, no per-minute fees: calls go over VoIP from your own server to your own phone. Don't want to run a server? The hosted version is at agentring.io (contact: info@agentring.io ).
Sound on. A real run with Claude Code, a Pixel 6 and the voice AI: a migration fails, Claude Code calls the locked phone, you decide, it carries on. The phone is a screen recording with the call audio (the ringtone was added), the terminal is redrawn from Claude Code's output, and only the waits were cut. Silent version: demo.gif .
Pre-release. Messages, calls on a locked phone, the voice AI, calling your agent from the app and the MCP server all work. So far it has been tested on one phone (Pixel 6, Android 16). Android only for now.
Your agent reaches you. It can send you a message, wait for your reply or call you ( send_message , get_replies , call ). On a call, a voice AI explains why the agent is calling, answers your questions and hands the transcript back.
You reach your agents. Tap "Call agent" in the app. The voice AI can ask your own agents for help mid-call. If one is slow, the call goes on and its answer arrives when it's ready, or as a message if you've already hung up.
Nothing gets lost. A missed call turns into a message you can answer from the notification.
Things people use it for: "run the migration and call me if anything fails" , "ask me before you deploy" , "what did CI say?" while driving, a daily call with your assistant about your inbox.
agentring doesn't care which harness you use: anything that speaks MCP can reach you, and anything you can run as a command can be consulted from a call.
Copy-paste setup for each: docs/agents.md .
relay (TypeScript): pairing, messages, call state, push, LiveKit tokens. Runs on your server behind Caddy.
LiveKit : the call audio, self-hosted in the same compose file.
daemon (Python): the agentring CLI, the MCP server and the voice AI. Runs next to your agents, behind NAT is fine.
Android app (Kotlin): QR pairing, the native call screen, messages.
The voice AI is the voice, your agent is the brain: a realtime speech model handles the conversation and hands real work to your agents. Pick the one you like:
Set AGENTRING_VOICE_PROVIDER in ~/.agentring/.env to use one for every call, from the CLI and from MCP. How they compare (latency, tool use) and how to add another one: docs/voice.md .
somewhere to run the relay: a Linux server with Docker and a domain name, or your own computer with Docker (the phone on the same Wi-Fi, or anywhere over Tailscale),
a free Firebase project, which is what makes a locked phone ring ( docs/firebase.md ),
a key for the voice AI: Gemini ( free tier ), or OpenAI, xAI (Grok) or Phonic ( providers ),
Get the app from Releases . The full tutorial, step by step for both options and with a troubleshooting table: docs/setup.md . If the phone doesn't ring when locked, it's usually the vendor's battery saver: docs/troubleshooting-oem.md .
Everything runs on your own servers and accounts. Messages and call metadata are stored on your relay. Push notifications go through your own Firebase project; they are signed, not encrypted, so Google's FCM can read pushed text. Call audio goes through your LiveKit server and, with the voice AI, to the provider you chose (Google, OpenAI, xAI or Phonic); on Google's free tier, Google may use that data to improve its products.
Over the phone, the voice AI acts on what it hears, so give it only the tools and agents you'd trust someone holding your phone with. Details and the threat model: SECURITY.md .
The voice AI needs a cloud realtime model (Gemini, OpenAI, Grok or Phonic); others, local ones included, plug in through RealtimeBackend .
CI builds the APK and runs an end-to-end test on an Android emulator against a real relay. See CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/release.md .
